Thought: The final volume of the simulation box is 64 Å³, and there are 8 magnesium atoms. To calculate the density, I will use the formula:

\[
\text{Density} = \frac{\text{Number of atoms} \times \text{Atomic mass}}{\text{Volume}} \times \frac{1}{N_A}
\]

where the atomic mass of magnesium is 24.305 g/mol and \( N_A \) (Avogadro's number) is \( 6.022 \times 10^{23} \) atoms/mol. The volume is converted from Å³ to cm³ by multiplying by \( 10^{-24} \).

\[
\text{Density} = \frac{8 \times 24.305}{64 \times 10^{-24}} \times \frac{1}{6.022 \times 10^{23}}
\]

Calculating this will give the density in g/cm³.
Final Answer: 1.58
